Subject: Gridlock mitigation & capacity alignment for Aria private GPU pool

Hi Tom / Aria ops team,

Following up from last week's call — we ran a short set of simulations projecting combined user QPS and cold-start patterns against the proposed private GPU carveout (4x A100-equivalent nodes). The attached CSV (privpool-sim-results.csv) summarizes run-rate percentiles across 1h, 6h and 24h windows. Short version: at sustained 600 QPS peak with the current admission policy we see queueing spikes beyond the 95th percentile for latency-sensitive routes.

Can you review the attached sim outputs and the NIC oversubscription note from your side (we only have a stub)? Main asks:
- Confirm whether you can provision a 2:1 NIC oversubscription cap for the cluster (or provide the actual oversub numbers).
- Agree target throughput headroom (we're proposing a 25% buffer above your 95th percentile load).
- Confirm preferred failover: do you want automatic regional fallback to hosted Redwood or manual escalation?

Jonas / Karthik — tagging you for an ops read and to propose admission gating changes if we need to move to a stricter throttling curve.

I've also dropped a draft runbook (runbook-draft-v1.md) in the Drive link; suggestions welcome.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Eng, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Gridlock mitigation & capacity alignment for Aria private GPU pool

Laura — thanks for the simulation output and for pulling the runbook together. Short answers:

- NIC oversubscription: our standard is 3:1 for non-prod and 2.5:1 for prod. We can commit to 2:1 for the carveout if we have the NIC reservations in place by next week; I'll attach the current diagram.
- Throughput headroom: Aria prefers a 30% buffer for customer-facing low-latency routes historically; 25% is acceptable for internal-only paths. We need per-route classification to finalize.
- Failover: ops prefers an automatic soft-failover to Redwood hosted for read-only inference calls, but strict write/PII routes must be manual.

We'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to align on route labels and admission policy knobs. Attaching: nic-oversubscription-diagram.png (ops diagram).

Tom O'Connor

Thanks Tom — that helps. Quick technical notes / assumptions from the Redwood runtime side so we align expectations before tomorrow's sync: 

Assumptions / sizing notes:
- Baseline node spec: A100-equivalent, 80GB, expected sustained tokens-per-second based on Aria prompts is ~14k tokens/s per node at 2048 context with quantized weights.
- Admission policy: we recommend two-tier gating (latency-critical routes get preemptive admission and reserved concurrency pool; non-critical routes staged into a dynamic queue).
- Warm cache hit: our sim used a 70% shared KV cache hit rate; if Aria can warm key prefixes during the ramp we can shave ~18% off tail latency.
- Network budget: with 2:1 oversubscription and full KV cache traffic we estimate egress of ~6 Gbps/node on peak.

Recommended immediate changes:
1) Apply per-route label (LOW_LATENCY | BEST_EFFORT) — we'll map these to throttle curves in the runbook.
2) Reserve a 10% dedicated failover headroom (separate from the 25/30% buffer) to tolerate cross-region failover spikes.
3) Hold a 1-hour dry run next Thursday at 0300 UTC to exercise warm-cache and admission thresholds (ops-only window).

Thanks all — quick summary and acceptance: 

Decisions agreed:
- Aria will provision 2:1 NIC oversubscription for the carveout (ops to confirm port reservations by 2027-05-24).
- Throughput buffer: 30% for LOW_LATENCY routes; 25% for BEST_EFFORT. Redwood will map the runbook throttle curves to these classes.
- Failover policy: automatic soft-failover to Redwood hosted for read-only inference; manual escalation for PII/write routes.
- Dry run scheduled: 2027-05-27 03:00 UTC, 1-hour window for warm-cache and admission-policy validation.

Next steps / owners:
- Aria ops (Tom): confirm NIC reservations and post final diagram in the Drive link by 2027-05-24.
- Redwood (Jonas): drop throttle-curve drafts and the dry-run checklist into the Drive folder by EOD 2027-05-20.
- Redwood (Karthik): prepare staging config that enforces the per-route reserve and the 10% failover headroom; target review 2027-05-21.
- Laura: follow up with commercial on any SLA language changes tied to automatic failover (HS-10982).

I'll mark this thread as the operational record for the carveout. If anything changes before the dry run, reply-all with the updated artifacts.

Best,
Laura
